measurement: US: CPS ORG BA+ and exhaustive non-BA headcount or matched usual-hours FTE. RoW: Eurostat lfsa_egaed, tertiary ED5-8 versus ED0-2+ED3_4, age 25-64, both sexes. Ratios can be data inputs after the skill/population convention is fixed.
limitation: Survey employment is directly observed for its stated population, but education is a skill bridge; US private for-profit is not exactly corporate, US age16+ differs from RoW25-64, and model efficiency/cohort units are not observed. Countries must be fixed before aggregation; G4/OECD-ex-US are not all RoW.

measurement: Conditional growth recovery: a_i=(N_{i,t+1}/N_{i,t}-1)/[(1-phi_i)H_i]. Active-entry alternative a_i=w_H/(N_i q_i).
limitation: Both use proxy knowledge and research inputs; a separately needs a labor unit and model period. The existing US free-entry-implied a_t is an I diagnostic, not an independent estimate of constant technology. RoW lacks matched wage levels.

measurement: Inverse markup; potentially estimate sector markup or invert vartheta=w_H phi H/(w_H phi H+D) under the exact model accounting.
limitation: Accounting gross margins, profit shares and markups differ once physical capital, fixed costs, taxes and retained earnings enter. No directly observed markup series identifies this parameter; conditional inversion requires matched structural sector.

measurement: Joint CES calibration with factor quantities, factor prices and augmentation scales.
limitation: alpha is not an observed skilled-labor income share. Only alpha A_X^(1-rho) and (1-alpha) A_L^(1-rho) enter the level CES; normalization is indispensable.

measurement: Elasticity is 1/rho_i; estimate from variation in relative production inputs and prices, conditional on augmentation/markup dynamics, or use an external structural restriction.
limitation: One factor share or wage premium cannot identify curvature; generic capital-labor elasticity is not this intermediate-input/unskilled-labor elasticity. Both countries are CES in the actual solver.

measurement: Unbalanced-US augmentation scale coefficients can be recovered only conditional on a CES inversion, knowledge scale, alpha,rho,vartheta and real-output/input units.
limitation: Neither R&D spending, R&D growth contribution, industry productivity nor sales/employee measures these two factor-specific scales.

measurement: Absorbing-branch coefficients require observed branch data and a structural production inversion or an explicit counterfactual restriction.
limitation: An all-u observed episode supplies no direct realization of the absorbing technology. Pre/post event comparisons require an independently justified regime mapping.

measurement: RoW augmentation levels jointly calibrated against harmonized labor, wages and output under the solver CES.
limitation: A weighted average of industry productivity is not a national factor-augmentation level. Currency/PPP, country membership, input quantities, wages and output universe must agree.

measurement: Elasticities of separately inferred augmentation with respect to a separately mapped knowledge index.
limitation: N and A are not directly observed; relative wage movements do not identify two elasticities. Setting A_X=N^xi and plotting that path imposes the mechanism rather than measuring it.

measurement: Maintained zero-exponent restrictions, not estimated or directly measured values.
limitation: Class L with fixed-restriction annotation; do not treat imposed zeros as measurement successes. Existing RoW R&D investment growth does not by itself falsify zero factor augmentation.

measurement: Normalize N_i0=1 or adopt an explicitly documented stock proxy and rebase.
limitation: A normalized state has no empirical level target. Patent stocks require office/residence/timing/depreciation/initial-stock conventions; R&D capital is a cost stock, not variety units.

measurement: Model law of motion yields a normalized state. Existing alternatives: Fed/BEA real-cost R&D stock sensitivity, depreciated USPTO/triadic stocks, or citation-adjusted patent index.
limitation: Patent grants/families are not varieties; R&D capital depreciates and includes valuation effects while the model stock does not. None measures the level exactly; proxy growth also depends on initialization and depreciation.

measurement: phi=1-R/H. US matched education-occupation CPS cell R=NRC intersection H is reproducible; formal business researcher/personnel FTE is a separate sensitivity.
limitation: NRC includes clinical/managerial/teaching work beyond innovation. NRC/total employment has wrong denominator. BERD full-population FTE divided by partial observed-hours CPS FTE is not fully matched. RoW task/skill cells require harmonization.

measurement: Conditional CES inversion: A_X=[vartheta alpha Y^rho/(w_H X^rho)]^[1/(rho-1)], A_L=[(1-alpha)Y^rho/(w_L L^rho)]^[1/(rho-1)], X=phi H.
limitation: Model-implied after parameters and empirical bridges, not an independent technology observation. Require Euler check w_H X/vartheta+w_L L=Y and do not renormalize incompatible shares. Singular at rho=1; highly sensitive nearby. Sector LP/TFP and R&D expenditure are different concepts.

measurement: Directly published candidate: resident corporate GVA from US IMA/BEA and OECD S11+S12 B1G. Deflate and use chosen geography/scope consistently.
limitation: Current model-to-data bridge remains I: corporate GVA includes own-account capitalized R&D whereas model production obeys Y=e+D-I. Sector/tax/capital accounting must be reconciled. D is appropriate for the specified corporate-GVA statistic itself, not automatic equality to model Y.

measurement: US: CPS matched skill hourly-earnings means/ratios; annual FTE compensation levels additionally use corporate compensation scaling. RoW OECD education earnings ratios are available irregularly.
limitation: Cash earnings and total compensation differ; mean hourly wage is not median weekly earnings. Whole-skilled-group wage is an opportunity-wage approximation to production workers. RoW ratios do not supply matched levels, hours or total wage bills.

measurement: Construct e=w_H H+w_L L from a matched employment, wage and time-unit universe; aggregate corporate compensation is an alternative scoped bridge.
limitation: Do not replace young-cohort labor income by GDP, disposable income or GVA. The existing US scaling forces the wage bill to compensation; it is not an independent test. RoW earnings-ratio data alone cannot recover e.

measurement: q_t=Q_t/N_t+1 and d_t=D_t/N_t; stock timing must be explicit. Distribution-excluding market price returns and dividend/total-return data supply observable indices/yields.
limitation: An arbitrary index level is not a price per model variety. Market-cap growth includes entry/issuance; dividend levels inherit the unknown variety unit. Price-return growth can be a D counterpart for a specified security universe, with composition and timing differences documented.

measurement: Equity capitalization and paid cash dividends are observable for a specified universe; potential D subcomponents. Model Q=N_next q, D=N d; keep end-period stock and within-period flow distinct.
limitation: The earlier AHP enterprise-value and free-cash-flow mappings are NOT automatically equity capitalization and cash dividends. Model has no physical capital/debt/taxes/retention at firm level; shareholder equity vs enterprise value, profits vs distributions and IPO timing must be reconciled.
